title: NEFT, RTGS, and IMPS Fund Transfer Rules
content: For NEFT transfers, collect beneficiary name, account number, IFSC code, and transfer amount. NEFT operates in half-hourly batches throughout the day and settles within 2 hours in normal circumstances. No minimum or maximum limit for NEFT. For RTGS, minimum transfer amount is INR 2 lakh with no upper limit. RTGS is real-time gross settlement and processes instantly during banking hours (7:00 AM to 6:00 PM on weekdays). For IMPS, transfers happen 24x7 including holidays with a per-transaction limit typically up to INR 5 lakh, subject to bank policy. NEFT charges at branch counter may apply as per the schedule of charges. RTGS charges vary by amount slab. IMPS charges depend on channel (branch, mobile, internet). Always verify beneficiary details before initiating transfer and provide the UTR/transaction reference number to the customer.

title: Cheque Book Issue, Stop Payment, and Return Charges
content: For cheque book issuance, verify account holder identity and account status. Standard cheque books of 10 or 25 leaves are available. First cheque book per financial year may be free depending on account variant; subsequent books attract charges as per the schedule. For stop payment requests, collect the cheque number, amount, payee name, and reason. Stop payment charges apply per cheque as per the schedule of charges and must be disclosed before processing. For cheque return due to insufficient funds, the presenting bank charges the payee and the issuing bank charges the drawer. Return charges for the drawer are typically INR 150 to INR 750 depending on cheque amount and bank policy. Always inform the customer about return charges and potential CIBIL impact before issuing cheques against uncertain balances.

title: Safe Deposit Locker Facility
content: For locker allotment, the customer must hold an active savings or current account with the branch. KYC must be current and complete. Locker rent is payable annually in advance and varies by locker size: small INR 1500 to INR 3000, medium INR 3000 to INR 6000, large INR 6000 to INR 12000 per annum depending on branch location and availability. Nomination is mandatory for locker facility as per RBI guidelines. The bank must not insist on any fixed deposit as a precondition for locker allotment. A waiting list is maintained when lockers are unavailable. For locker break-open in case of lost keys, charges include lock replacement cost plus a break-open fee. The procedure requires the customer's written request, identity verification, and must be done in the presence of a bank official and the locker holder. Annual locker access register must be maintained.

title: Recurring Deposit Opening and Rules
content: For recurring deposit (RD) opening, collect the monthly installment amount (minimum typically INR 100), tenure (6 months to 10 years), linked savings account for auto-debit, nominee details, and maturity instructions. Interest rate is the same as the FD rate for the equivalent tenure. If the customer misses installments, a penalty of INR 1.50 per INR 100 per month of default may apply subject to bank policy. RD can be closed prematurely after 3 months of opening in most cases; interest will be recalculated at the rate applicable for the completed tenure minus penalty. Partial withdrawal is not permitted in standard RD. Loan against RD is available up to 90% of the deposit value at RD rate plus 1% to 2%. Always disclose penalty and premature closure rules before opening.

title: Public Provident Fund (PPF) Account Rules
content: For PPF account opening, the customer must be a resident Indian individual. Only one PPF account per individual is permitted. Minimum annual deposit is INR 500 and maximum is INR 1.50 lakh per financial year. Deposits can be made in lump sum or up to 12 installments per year. PPF has a 15-year lock-in period with extension option in blocks of 5 years. Partial withdrawal is permitted from the 7th financial year onwards, limited to 50% of the balance at the end of the 4th preceding year or the preceding year, whichever is lower. Loan against PPF is available from the 3rd to the 6th financial year. Current interest rate is notified quarterly by the Government of India. PPF is EEE (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt) under Section 80C. The customer must be informed that the interest rate is subject to quarterly revision by the government.

title: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) Account Rules
content: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana account can be opened for a girl child below 10 years of age by the natural or legal guardian. Maximum two accounts for two girl children per family (exception for twins or triplets as the third). Minimum deposit is INR 250 per financial year, maximum is INR 1.50 lakh. The account matures 21 years from the date of opening or upon marriage of the girl child after age 18, whichever is earlier. Deposits are required for the first 15 years only. Partial withdrawal of up to 50% of the balance is allowed after the girl child turns 18 years for education or marriage expenses. The interest rate is notified quarterly by the Government of India. Tax benefit under Section 80C applies. Required documents include birth certificate of the girl child, identity and address proof of the guardian, and photographs.

title: Senior Citizen Savings Scheme (SCSS) Rules
content: Senior Citizen Savings Scheme is available to individuals aged 60 years and above, or 55 years and above for those who have retired under a voluntary or special voluntary retirement scheme. Maximum deposit limit is INR 30 lakh per individual. The account has a 5-year tenure with one extension of 3 years permitted within 1 year of maturity. Interest is payable quarterly and is credited to the linked savings account. Current interest rate is notified quarterly by the Government of India. Premature closure is permitted after 1 year with a 1.5% penalty and after 2 years with a 1% penalty deducted from the deposit amount. TDS applies if interest exceeds INR 50,000 per financial year. Tax benefit under Section 80C applies for the deposit amount. Required documents include age proof, PAN, Aadhaar, and retirement proof if aged 55-59.

title: Insurance Product Guardrails — Mis-selling Prevention
content: Staff must never guarantee returns on insurance or ULIP products. Insurance is a risk cover product, not an investment. Never compare insurance returns with fixed deposit rates. Never say the premium is a one-time payment unless the policy is genuinely single-premium. Always disclose the free-look period (15 days for offline, 30 days for online policies). Always explain surrender charges and lock-in period clearly. Never bundle insurance as a mandatory requirement for loan disbursement or account opening — this is a regulatory violation. Always provide the IRDAI-mandated benefit illustration to the customer before purchase. If the customer asks about insurance, explain that the bank acts as a corporate agent and the insurance is underwritten by the partner insurance company. Never use the words 'guaranteed returns' for market-linked products.

title: Nomination Rules for Accounts, FDs, and Lockers
content: Nomination is strongly recommended for all deposit accounts, FDs, RDs, and locker facilities as per RBI guidelines. For new account openings, obtain nominee details during the opening process itself. The nominee can be any individual; if a minor is nominated, a guardian must be designated. Nomination can be registered, changed, or cancelled at any time by the account holder by submitting the prescribed form (DA1 for registration, DA2 for cancellation or change). For joint accounts, nomination is effective only after the death of all joint holders. The nominee receives the deposit amount as a trustee and not as a beneficial owner — this must be communicated clearly. For locker nomination, Form SL1 is used. Maintain nomination register updated at the branch level.

title: ATM and Cash Services at Branch Counter
content: For ATM-related queries: daily ATM withdrawal limit is typically INR 20,000 to INR 1,00,000 depending on card variant. If the customer reports ATM cash not dispensed but account debited, lodge a complaint immediately in the ATM dispute module and provide the complaint reference number. Auto-reversal happens within T+5 days; if not reversed, the bank must credit the amount within T+5 days as per RBI guidelines. For cash deposit at branch, amounts above INR 50,000 require PAN. Cash transactions above INR 10 lakh in a financial year are reported to the Income Tax department. For cash withdrawal above INR 50,000, verify identity and maintain CTR records. Always count cash in front of the customer and provide a receipt.

title: Internet Banking and Mobile Banking Support
content: For internet banking registration at branch, the customer needs an active savings or current account with a registered mobile number. Provide the temporary username and password in a sealed envelope or via registered mobile OTP. Transaction limits for internet banking are set by the bank and can be modified by the customer within allowed limits. For mobile banking app registration, the customer must have an active debit card and registered mobile number. UPI registration can be done through the bank's mobile app using the debit card for authentication. For password reset requests, verify customer identity using debit card details, registered mobile OTP, and one identity document. Never share passwords or OTPs over phone or email. Advise customers to change the temporary password immediately upon first login.

title: Credit Score and CIBIL Enquiry Guidelines
content: Staff can check the customer's CIBIL score in CBS only with the customer's explicit consent and for a legitimate business purpose (loan application, credit card application). Never disclose the exact credit score to the customer; instead, inform them whether their score meets the bank's lending criteria. The customer can obtain their own CIBIL report for free once a year from the CIBIL website. If the customer disputes any entry in their credit report, guide them to raise a dispute directly with CIBIL or the concerned lender. Staff must not guarantee loan approval based on CIBIL score alone, as multiple factors affect credit assessment. Never discuss another customer's credit information.

title: Savings and Current Account Closure Procedure
content: For account closure, verify the account holder's identity using PAN, Aadhaar, and registered mobile OTP. Ensure all cheques issued have been cleared and no cheques are pending. Collect the unused cheque leaves and debit card from the customer. Ensure all standing instructions, ECS mandates, and auto-debit instructions linked to the account are cancelled. Close any linked RD, PPF, or other subsidiary accounts first. For zero-balance BSBD accounts, no charges apply for closure. For other account variants, account closure charges may apply as per the schedule of charges if the account is closed within one year of opening. Transfer the remaining balance to another account or issue a demand draft. Provide an account closure acknowledgement to the customer. Maintain records as per the bank's record retention policy.

title: Demand Draft Issue and Cancellation
content: For demand draft issuance, collect the payee name, amount, payable-at city, and purpose. Demand drafts above INR 50,000 must be by account debit only (not cash) as per RBI guidelines. DD commission charges apply as per the schedule of charges and must be disclosed before issuance. For DD cancellation, the customer must submit the original DD along with a cancellation request letter. Verify the DD has not been presented for payment. Refund the DD amount after deducting cancellation charges to the customer's account. For duplicate DD issuance in case of lost DD, the customer must submit an indemnity bond and a non-payment certificate request must be obtained from the payable branch. Processing time for duplicate DD is typically 15 to 30 days.

title: Standing Instructions and Auto-Debit Mandates
content: For standing instruction setup, collect the debit account number, beneficiary details, amount (fixed or variable), frequency (weekly, monthly, quarterly), start and end dates, and purpose. Standing instruction charges may apply per execution as per the schedule of charges. For ECS/NACH mandates, the customer must sign the mandate form with account details and maximum debit amount. NACH mandates can be registered online through net banking or at the branch. To cancel a standing instruction or NACH mandate, the customer must submit a written request or cancel through net banking. Processing of cancellation takes 1 to 2 working days. Always confirm the next execution date with the customer. If a standing instruction fails due to insufficient balance, failure charges may apply.
